hypothesis: Long-horizon trend measures (trailing 7-day, 30-day, 90-day returns; distance of price from its 50-day and 200-day averages) carry DIRECTIONAL information about forward returns at the longer horizons (72h, 168h), consistent with the well-documented time-series momentum effect at monthly scales -- something the current 'trend' category (about 10 days of history) cannot see.
acceptance_criterion: PRE-REGISTERED before running. Same directional rule as E003: Spearman(feature, return_H) block-bootstrap 95% interval excludes zero with the same sign in BOTH exploration and validation. Magnitude rule as E003 (|rho| >= 0.10 both periods). Descriptive only: mean 24h/168h forward return by 30-day trend regime (uptrend / sideways / downtrend) in each period.
feature_version: research features v1: ret_168h, ret_720h, ret_2160h, dist_sma_1200, dist_sma_4800

target.definition: signed forward return (direction) and absolute forward return (magnitude)
target.outcome: close of candle opening at as_of+H

point_in_time: trailing functions of candles with as_of <= t on a complete hourly grid (gaps blank the window); tests/test_features_point_in_time.py. The 4,800h window means the first ~200 days of data have no value for dist_sma_4800.
notes: Caution stated in advance: validation (2024-01 -> 2025-06) is dominated by one long uptrend (ETF approval). A trend feature can look good there for the same reason buy-and-hold does. That is why the criterion also requires the exploration period (which contains two bear markets) and why the per-year signs are reported.
